notes_for_us: Drifting is a driving style, not a genre, and the Racing-versus-Simulation boundary turns on a finish condition the prompt never states. The skill forbids asking how the game is won, and the sanctioned substitute - is there an end or is it endless - is exactly the question needed, so the rules did hold. But the answer decides both the genre and P6 versus P0, which is a lot of weight on an inference.

There is no drift-specific geometry anywhere: no wide-radius corner, no skidpad, no touge. Racing's options are all about lanes, laps and barriers, which assume you are trying to go fast in a straight line rather than sideways.

'Baseplate' came up twice in this batch as the stated ground of the build. It is Roblox's default flat grey plate and the users saying it clearly mean 'plain, empty, no terrain' - which is a real instruction to the image model and has no home.

Four preset options against three things the user said. Circuit Racing brought a starting grid, lap detection, guardrails and turnarounds off a fourteen-word prompt, and only the guardrails are safe bets for a drift map.

notes_for_us: The genre index note on the '+1 speed' family did exactly its job on a prompt that looks nothing like a simulator: keys, money and speed read as a clicker only because that note names the pattern. Without it this lands on Obby and picks up a P6.

The map is shaped like a real-world object, and nothing in the shape system can say that. tier-ladder captures the progression and loses the keyboard entirely; the keyboard survives only as free text and as theme, and it is the one thing the user actually described.

station-training is the only row for the pressable key, and its wording assumes a treadmill or weight rack - a stat station you stand on. A keyboard of hundreds of individually pressable keys is a grid of them, and there is no way to say how many.
Second non-English prompt in this batch, and both were the hardest to classify. The skill has no guidance on translating a prompt before matching against an index written in English keywords.

notes_for_us: This prompt is a copy-pasted conversation with another chatbot, containing two complete and unrelated game designs plus the bot's replies. Nothing in layout-intake says which one to build. I took the last request on the ordinary reading that the newest ask wins, but that is my rule, not the skill's, and the earlier game would produce a completely different map. This is worth an explicit instruction - transcript prompts are clearly common in this set.

A theft loop needs geometry the system has no words for: something displayed, somewhere it can be seen from outside, and a way in that is not the owner's door. plot-isolated explicitly describes plots that never overlap a neighbour, which is the opposite of the game.
Display furniture is missing across the board - shelves, plinths, cases, racks. This is the third prompt in the batch wanting objects arranged to be looked at with nothing to hold them.

The rarity roster is 53 toys in six tiers and it produced no layout at all, correctly. But the collection book and the leaderboards are UI surfaces the handoff cannot route anywhere except mechanics, where the layout stream will ignore them.
